items.title: Player interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2012
items.q: you mentioned that in colleges it’s like jazz starts with Charlie Parker.

ctx.x: so I mean there was some appreciation in every home, there was some appreciation of music. I mean people appreciated it, even if they weren’t going to be professional musicians, most people maybe had experiences with starting in a band program, or they could at least have some basic understanding to what it would take to become on the level that we know some of our greatest professional musicians are. And so you did have some appreciation there. But now it’s just all sports it seems. And I’m not knocking the…
Is it hard to teach someone to play in the style of a New Orleans musician? What I’m trying to get at is, you mentioned that in colleges it’s like jazz starts with Charlie Parker.
